summary: Audited mac.dream_cycle_classifier skill-area detection and test coverage. Implementation is functionally correct with one notable regex bug (unescaped dot in hermes.skill pattern). Identified 7 concrete test gaps for the repair child task.

_SKILL_PATTERNS_notes: Pattern (r'\bhermes.skill\b', 'skill') — BUG: dot is unescaped; matches 'hermesXskill', 'hermes skill', 'hermes-skill', etc. Should be r'\bhermes\.skill\b'. In practice the first generic pattern already catches any text containing the literal word 'skill', so false-positives from the bug do not break existing tests; however tests that verify hermes.skill as a *distinct* signal from the generic pattern are absent.
_match_patterns_notes: All matching patterns fire against the combined text (_combined_text) of summary + kind + scope + observations + record_type_count keys + retrieval query_terms.
Multiple patterns that share the same area_name are correctly aggregated into one area hit dict; their distinct regex strings appear in the 'signals' list.
The _generic_tool suppression logic is correct: if any specific tool pattern matches, the generic '\btool\b' entry is dropped.

Area hits for 'skill' are always emitted as a single dict (all skill-area patterns map to area_name='skill'), so signal_count = len(matched_patterns). This is key for _confidence_for: two skill-specific patterns firing in the same text will produce signal_count=2 → medium confidence even with only one evidence record.

_confidence_for_logic.rule_2: candidate_confidence=='high' AND signal_count >= 2 AND unique_record_types >= 1 → high (0.90)

_confidence_for_notes: Rule ordering is deterministic and correct. The high-path conditions are checked before medium; no overlap.
signal_count is per-area (len of matched signals for that area), NOT global across all areas.

When multiple SKILL patterns co-fire on the same text (e.g. 'hermes.skill' + 'skill_command'), signal_count ≥ 2 → medium even with 1 evidence record. This is correct per spec but is only incidentally exercised by tests (not explicitly targeted).

coverage_gaps.description: hermes.skill pattern never individually tested. The test test_single_signal_skill_reference_detected uses 'skill bundle' (a space-separated phrase), which only triggers the generic \bskill[s]?\b pattern — not \bhermes.skill\b. No test exercises the hermes.skill pattern in isolation or alongside the generic pattern.
coverage_gaps.regex_bug: The pattern r'\bhermes.skill\b' has an unescaped dot, so it also matches 'hermesXskill' and 'hermes skill'. A test using 'hermes.skill' in the summary would currently pass (both literal match and false-positive match fire), but a test asserting that 'hermesXskill' does NOT trigger the hermes.skill pattern would fail, revealing the bug.

coverage_gaps.description: curator pattern never individually tested. It appears only as a co-occurring keyword inside test_high_confidence_candidate_plus_multi_signal_types (line 225), mixed with skill_bundle and terminal_tool. No standalone test asserts that 'curator' alone triggers a skill area.
skill_command pattern never individually tested. Not referenced anywhere in the test file.
skill_utils pattern never individually tested. Not referenced anywhere in the test file.
skill_preprocessing pattern never individually tested. Not referenced anywhere in the test file.

Single-evidence → medium upgrade via two co-firing skill signals is not explicitly tested for skill areas. The test test_single_signal_with_two_evidence_upgrades_to_medium covers this for a tool area (web_search). When two skill-specific patterns co-fire on the same text (e.g. 'hermes.skill' and 'skill_command' both present, signal_count=2), _confidence_for returns medium with only 1 evidence record. This path is exercised by test_high_confidence_candidate_plus_multi_signal_types but only as a side-effect at high confidence (2 evidence + high candidate). An explicit skill-area medium-via-two-signals test is missing.

High-confidence skill path is only exercised inside test_high_confidence_candidate_plus_multi_signal_types, which uses a mixed summary involving terminal_tool (a tool area). No test verifies that skill areas alone reach high confidence via the candidate.confidence=='high' + signal_count>=2 rule (rule 2) or the 3-evidence rule (rule 1) for pure skill content.

No test directly asserts that when both skill and tool signals appear in the same candidate, both area types appear independently in the report with correct area_type values. test_high_confidence_candidate_plus_multi_signal_types implicitly exercises this but does not inspect individual area_type fields for skill + tool co-occurrence.

The unescaped dot bug in r'\bhermes.skill\b' is untested. No test supplies a string like 'hermesXskill' or 'hermes skill' (without a literal dot) to verify that only hermes.skill (with literal dot) triggers that pattern. Existing tests do not distinguish between the generic \bskill[s]?\b catch-all and the hermes.skill-specific pattern.

implementation_correctness_verdict.details: The classifier logic (pattern tables, _match_patterns, _confidence_for, classify_candidate) is correct and self-consistent with the module docstring. All 27 existing tests pass. One correctness issue exists: the hermes.skill regex has an unescaped dot (should be r'\bhermes\.skill\b'). This is a latent false-positive bug — currently harmless in practice because the generic \bskill[s]?\b pattern fires first on real inputs, but it will silently over-count the hermes.skill signal on any text containing 'hermesXskill' or the two-word phrase 'hermes skill'. The bug is exercisable via tests but requires a test that distinguishes the two patterns.

recommended_tests_for_repair_child.description: Supply a summary containing 'hermes.skill' (with literal dot) and assert area_type='skill' is detected. Check that the signals list includes the hermes.skill pattern string, not just the generic skill[s]? pattern.

Supply a summary containing 'hermes skill' (space, no dot) but NOT the bare word 'skill' elsewhere. Verify that the hermes.skill specific pattern is NOT in the signals list; only the generic \bskill[s]?\b fires. This test will fail against the current unescaped-dot regex, confirming the bug.
Supply a summary containing only 'curator' (e.g. 'curator service encountered an error'). Assert area_type='skill' is present and area_name='skill'. Evidence count=1 → confidence='low'.
Supply a summary with 'skill_command was invoked'. Assert skill area hit with signals containing the skill_command pattern. 1 evidence → low confidence.
Supply a summary with 'skill_utils function returned error'. Assert skill area hit with signals containing the skill_utils? pattern. 1 evidence → low confidence.
Supply a summary with 'skill_preprocessing pipeline failed'. Assert skill area hit with signals containing the skill_preprocessing pattern. 1 evidence → low confidence.

Supply a summary containing both 'hermes.skill' and 'skill_command' (two distinct skill patterns). evidence_count=1. Assert that the skill area has confidence='medium' (0.65) because signal_count=2 triggers rule 4 in _confidence_for.
Supply a summary with only skill content (e.g. 'curator processed skill bundles using skill_utils'). evidence_count=3. Assert overall_confidence='high' and all skill areas have confidence='high'.

Supply candidate with confidence='high', evidence_count=2, 2 distinct record types, summary containing 'skill_command and skill_utils conflict'. Assert skill area confidence='high' via rule 2 of _confidence_for.

Supply a summary with 'skill_command invoked terminal_tool'. Assert that report['areas'] contains at least one area with area_type='skill' AND at least one with area_type='tool', verifying co-occurrence isolation.
